Draw a figure's point layers with WebGL

Source: R/plot_helpers.R
auto_webgl.Rd

SVG slows down badly with many points, where WebGL does not. This switches the figure's point traces (scatter traces drawn as markers only: jitter, the points of a scatter plot) to scattergl once, together, they hold at least threshold points. Lines, filled areas, boxes, and violins stay SVG, so they stay vector in SVG downloads; only the switched points become an embedded image there. Unlike plotly::toWebGL(), which switches every trace.

Usage

auto_webgl(fig, threshold = .webgl_threshold(), overlays = FALSE)

Arguments

fig

A plotly figure, built or as plotly::ggplotly() returns it.

threshold

Point count at and above which the points switch.

overlays

Logical; also switch unfilled line traces, for lines that must stay on top of the points.

Value

The figure.

Details

WebGL canvases sit above SVG traces, so a line drawn over the points (an ellipse, a contour) would end up beneath them. Set overlays = TRUE to switch a figure's unfilled line traces with its points, which keeps their order. The points alone decide whether the threshold is reached, and filled traces stay SVG either way.

Pair it with webgl_input(). The default threshold is 5,000 points, or options(VizModules.webgl.threshold = n).

See also

webgl_input()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

fig <- plotly::plot_ly(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100), type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
fig <- plotly::plotly_build(fig)
auto_webgl(fig, threshold = 50)$x$data[[1]]$type
#> [1] "scattergl"
